chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Rabaat, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was praying, and Aisha was sleeping, lying sideways in front of him, and she was not praying.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman praying parallel to a man if she is not praying?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) patience and flexibility in prayer by allowing Aisha to sleep directly in front of him without invalidating his Salah. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary evidence for the permissibility of a woman praying parallel to a man, particularly illustrating that the presence of a non-praying or sleeping individual in the prayer space does not necessarily constitute a defect (nuqs) in the man's prayer.
